title_content.content: Key Takeaways from Inaugural MS Biopharma Symposium

paragraph_content.content: - Global recognition of China innovation is moving beyond engineering to the 2.0 Era - more novel modalities, disease areas and next-gen technologies.
• Correspondingly, BD deal models are broadening from pure out-licensing to NewCo, Co-co (co-commercialization) and strategic partnerships.
- Clean IP, corporate structure and globally translatable clinical development strategies are additional factors to consider in preparing for globalization.
- AI-driven drug discovery is shifting from platform narrative to asset generation.
- Hengrui is an example of China biopharma globalization, underpinned by end-to-end development capabilities and monetized via versatile BD models.

title_content.content: TCM: Still Going Through a Rough Patch

paragraph_content.content: - Consumption demand, input cost, government reimbursement controls and tender price cuts continued to hamper earnings performance.
- The 2025 pilot program permitting the use of imported bezoar has driven a sharp decline in natural bezoar prices, from RMB1.65mn/kg at the start of 2025 to Rmb520k/kg in June 2026.
- TCM companies provide the most stable cash flows and highest dividend payouts in China Healthcare space. Some examples include Jiangzhong, Dong E E Jiao and Yunnan Baiyao.

chart_footnote.content: Source: WIND, MS.

chart_caption.content: TCM A-shares aggregate dividend payout ratios (2020-2024)

chart_footnote.content: Source: FactSet; MS. Note: Dividend payout ratios are calculated using data from 72 constituents.

paragraph_content.content: - April SSSG declined 1.0% YoY, while year-to-date SSSG was flat (up 0.3% YoY). Lingering factors such as regulatory spot checks, soft consumption and price cuts all played a part.
- Net store closures in 2025 amounted to ~22,000, bringing the total number of pharmacies to 680,000 by year-end.

- Commentaries still pointed to a further industry-wide 30% contraction by store numbers from peak (~700,000) over three to five years, with closures concentrated in small- to mid-sized pharmacies and lower-tier cities.

- Leading chains are back in expansion mode through M&A, franchising and self-operated (2026 target: DSL +3,000, Yifeng +2,000, LBX +2,100), with franchising as the primary source of growth given its asset-light profile and fast access to underpenetrated markets.

- Policy direction is shifting toward higher compliance standards and a more integrated role for pharmacies in China's medical system. Ongoing policy trends include: end-to-end drug traceability, integrated healthcare centre transition, whitelisting items for reimbursement through personal accounts, etc.

We expect earnings growth in 2026 to be driven by cost optimization through: 1) pruning down of low efficiency stores; and 2) AI initiatives to improve operational efficiency. Top line will depend on sales of TCMs, private labels and franchising.
